dead_ends.approach: Run npm ci while the local Vinext preview still held native modules open.
dead_ends.why_failed: Windows returned EPERM on lightningcss; stopping the preview made the unchanged clean-install command pass.

dead_ends.approach: Use an alternate or locally installed browser to close G5.
dead_ends.why_failed: The controller reported no backend and the Browser/Sites rules prohibit ad-hoc standalone browser fallback.

dead_ends.approach: printing em-dash and section-sign in OpenHawk CLI output on Windows
dead_ends.why_failed: cp1252 terminal mojibakes them to replacement chars; use ASCII in runtime-printed strings (the recurring Windows lesson) - comments/docstrings are fine

dead_ends.approach: backtick path 'adapters/doctrine_adapter.py' in the MAPLE integration doc to name a proposed upstream module
dead_ends.why_failed: lint's REF_RE reads adapters/-prefixed backtick paths as corpus refs and failed the suite; prefix upstream paths with the package name (maple/adapters/...)

dead_ends.approach: trusting a piped exit code (verify | grep | head) as gate evidence
dead_ends.why_failed: pipeline exit code came from head, not doctrine_verify - a FAIL could read as 0; capture to a log file and take the runner's own exit code

learned.claim: The source dashboard now has lockfile, lint, typecheck, build/test, and moderate-audit CI gates on Ubuntu and Windows.
Adding an explicit TypeScript gate exposed an undeclared Cloudflare Fetcher type that production builds had not reported.
The dashboard workflow is source-only; Doctrine consumer installs continue receiving only the dashboard-agnostic doctrine.yml.
